title: Recover some coverage on account DB wrappers and membership ops
body:
## Summary

The arch-refactor merge dropped CI coverage 94.95% → 89.02%. This PR adds 8 targeted unit tests covering paths the refactor introduced without tests — three new per-account-DB repositories and the lightweight column-flip behavior of `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive` / `unarchive`.

## What's tested

`database/account/push_registrations.rs` (2 tests)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_registration` — the wrapper's only added behavior is binding `account_pubkey`; this locks it in.
- `separate_accounts_have_independent_per_account_dbs` — the per-account-DB architectural invariant (post-#786 split); two repos over distinct account DBs must not see each other's rows. Inner `PushRegistration` tests share one pool and can't express this.

`database/account/group_push_tokens.rs` (1 test)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_token` — pubkey-binding contract on the wrapper.

`database/account/published_key_packages.rs` (1 test)
- `mark_key_material_deleted_by_id_flips_one_row_only` — contrapositive regression guard for PR #822: the by-id variant must NOT cascade to dual-kind twins. A future refactor that "fixes consistency" by accidentally hash_ref-scoping the by-id variant trips this test. No inner-test analogue.

`accounts_groups.rs` (4 tests)
- `test_archive_sets_archived_at`, `test_archive_is_idempotent`, `test_unarchive_clears_archived_at`, `test_unarchive_on_unarchived_chat_is_no_op` — lightweight column-flip tests for `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive`/`unarchive` via the `get_or_create(None)` path. Distinct from the existing `chat_list.rs` archive tests, which spin up a real MLS group via `create_group(...)` and assert stream emit; these target the wrapper's mutation contract without the MLS setup cost.

## What's deliberately not in this PR

- **Wrapper pure-delegation roundtrip tests.** Pure pass-through `Ok(Inner::fn(...).await?)` calls add coverage but no signal — the inner SQL has its own tests. Per the user rule "tests that really increase coverage, not tests that are not testing anything," these were dropped after review.
- **Hash_ref-scoped twin tests** for `mark_consumed` / `mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref`. Already covered by the inner tests `test_mark_consumed_updates_timestamp_for_twins` and `test_mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref_marks_twins` in `database/published_key_packages.rs`.
- **Archive/unarchive emit-frame tests.** Already covered at the heavyweight level by `test_archive_chat_emits_to_both_stream_channels` in `chat_list.rs`.
- **Schema-shadowing fix.** The account-DB tests currently hand-roll a `DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE` because `AccountDatabase::new` uses `open_without_migrations` (running the full timeline here would require wiring a shared pool). Filed for a separate follow-up — a `setup_account_db_with_migrations()` helper that the whole `account/*.rs` suite can migrate to.

## Coverage math caveat

Coverage probably lands around 90–92% local lib — clears the post-merge CI baseline of 89.02% but doesn't recover the full pre-merge 94.95%. The remaining gap is structural: arch-refactor genuinely deleted code paths that had coverage, and shallow tests aren't the right fix.

## Verification

- `just check-fmt` ✓
- `just check-clippy` ✓
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::database::account` — 55 pass
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::accounts_groups::tests` — all pass including the 4 new archive/unarchive

title: Investigate slow initial startup time (~15s)
body:
## Context

Initial app startup currently feels too slow. The observed startup time is roughly 15 seconds before the app is ready.

This issue is to investigate where that time is being spent inside `whitenoise-rs` initialization and startup work.

## Details

Areas that look worth profiling first:

- `Whitenoise::initialize_whitenoise()` overall startup path
- startup cache sync work such as `sync_message_cache_on_startup()`
- relay / control-plane initialization
- scheduled task startup
- database migrations or other one-time initialization work
- any blocking network calls or waits happening before the UI can proceed

Questions to answer:

- what are the biggest contributors to the ~15 second startup time
- how much of that cost is local CPU / I/O vs network waiting
- which work is truly required before the app becomes usable
- which work can be deferred until after first render / first usable state
- whether there is a measurable difference between first startup, cold startup, and subsequent launches

## Outcome

Produce a breakdown of startup cost and identify concrete follow-up optimizations.

Possible outcomes:

- move non-critical startup work off the critical path
- defer sync or maintenance tasks until after initial readiness
- add instrumentation / timing logs around initialization phases
- split one-time setup from normal launch work
- open targeted follow-up issues once the hotspots are known

## Additional context

There is already app-side DX work around startup behavior in `marmot-protocol/whitenoise`, but this issue is specifically about the Rust core initialization path because that is likely where a large part of the delay lives.

title: feat(frb): move FRB codegen into whitenoise-rs
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/fe803ca425e08f2909f8cd21fb03cb058c6ba39e24b854f51ae047c3c37d5384.png)

## What changed

FRB codegen runs in whitenoise-rs CI now. Every codeowner push to `master` regenerates the Dart bindings and pushes them to a dedicated `flutter-package` orphan branch. The Flutter app consumes that branch as a normal git dependency.

No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` runs on the Flutter side. No more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Added on master

- `crates/whitenoise-frb/`: the FFI wrapper crate. Workspace member, path dep on the parent `whitenoise` crate. Sources ported from the in-flight `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch (post-singleton-removal refactor).
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: root config; `dart_output: .frb-staging/lib/src/rust`.
- `scripts/frb-{stage,generate,check}.sh` and matching `just` recipes.
- `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`: codeowner-gated workflow that clones the orphan branch, regenerates, vendors the wrapper crate (rewrites the `whitenoise` dep from path to a git rev), and force-pushes the orphan branch when something changed.
- `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`: architecture, bootstrap, rollout sequence, Flutter-side cleanup checklist.

## NOT on master

The Flutter package shape (pubspec, cargokit, platform glue, generated dart, vendored rust source) lives only on the `flutter-package` orphan branch (no shared history with master). Local dev uses `.frb-staging/` (gitignored) as a worktree of that branch.

## Codeowner gate

Hardcoded allowlist in the workflow (mirror `.github/CODEOWNERS`): @erskingardner, @dannym-arx, @mubarakcoded, @jgmontoya. Non-codeowner pushes skip the codegen job; the orphan branch stays put.

## Coordination with the Flutter side

This PR's wrapper sources came from `whitenoise.move-frb-out`'s `rust/src/api/`. Once this PR lands and CI updates the orphan branch, a separate Flutter-side PR (per `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`) removes `rust/`, `rust_builder/`, `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`, `lib/src/rust/`, the `just generate` recipe, and switches the pubspec to a git dep on the `flutter-package` ref.

## Verified locally

- `cargo check -p rust_lib_whitenoise`: wrapper compiles.
- `just frb-check`: wrapper passes clippy under `-D warnings`.
- `just check-fmt`: fmt clean.
- `just frb-stage && just frb-generate`: end-to-end codegen run; idempotent on rerun.

## Not yet verified

- First `workflow_dispatch` run end-to-end (proves the orphan-branch update path).
- Flutter app consuming the orphan branch via `flutter pub get`.

## Suggested rollout

1. Run the workflow once via `workflow_dispatch` to prove the codegen and orphan-branch update path.
2. Verify by cloning the orphan branch and running `flutter pub get` in a throwaway Flutter app.
3. Land the Flutter cleanup PR.

Draft until step 1 and 2 are green.

A marmot used to scurry between two burrows ferrying every Rust API change by paw. Now the burrow does it.

title: fix(frb): make pubkey required in subscribe_to_group_messages (remove unreachable None path)
body:
## Summary

In `crates/whitenoise-frb/src/api/messages.rs`, `subscribe_to_group_messages` declares `pubkey: Option<String>` but immediately requires it — the `None` path is unreachable and the FRB API contract is misleading.

This was intentionally left as-is in PR #827 (move-out migration) to keep the generated Dart bindings identical to the `whitenoise.move-frb-out` branch and avoid coupling a signature change to a Flutter callsite update in the same merge.

## Work items

- [ ] Change `pubkey: Option<String>` → `pubkey: String` in `subscribe_to_group_messages`
- [ ] Replace `parsed_pubkey` / `subscription_pubkey` Option dance with a direct `PublicKey::parse(&pubkey)?`
- [ ] Remove the unreachable `None => subscription.initial_messages` arm
- [ ] Re-run FRB codegen (`just frb-generate`) and force-push the `flutter-package` orphan branch
- [ ] Update Flutter callsite(s) that pass an `Option` for this parameter

## References

- PR introducing the code: #827 (comment: https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/827#discussion_r3233923386)
- Requested by: @dannym-arx

title: [codex] Enforce deletion author checks
body: ## Summary Fixes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#94. This enforces the NIP-09 deletion authorization rule inside MLS group message handling: - Require the kind-5 deletion author to match the cached target message/reaction author before mutating local cache state. - Preserve kind-5 deletion rows as audit/orphan records, but reject unauthorized orphan replay when the target message later arrives. - Add an author predicate to `AggregatedMessage::mark_deleted` so the DB update is guarded too. - Apply the same author check to outgoing optimistic deletion handling so local UI state cannot be rewritten for another author's target. ## Verification - Confirmed the issue was real with a red regression test: `test_handle_mls_message_rejects_cross_author_deletion` failed before the fix because the target was marked deleted. - `just test-unit` passed: 1737 unit tests + doctests. - `just precommit-quick` passed. - `just docker-up` passed. - `just precommit` passed, including integration tests. - `just docker-down` completed after validation. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Deletions are now author-scoped—only the original message/reaction author can mark their content deleted * Orphaned-deletion tracking and cascade rollback respect author scoping and restore targets from stored mappings * Outgoing deletion handling skips mismatched targets and avoids incorrect "last message deleted" signals * **Refactor** * Emission ordering improved: snapshot pre-mutation last-message is used to decide chat-list updates * **Tests** * Added coverage for cross-author deletions, orphaned-deletion application, cascade rollback, and reaction scenarios [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/pull/803)
